# Gamemodes
Monolith has several different gamemodes, each featuring different factions, different durations and different gameloops.
## Insurgency (TSF|PDV, 6hr)
[italic][color=yellow]The Trans-Solarian Federation's efforts to colonise the Colossus sector are put into danger by a theocratic insurgency, with civilians caught in the crossfire.[/color][/italic]
[bold]Insurgency[/bold] is the standard Monolith experience.
The Trans-Solarian Federation Marine Corps has just dealt a severe blow to the primary military arm of the Phaethon Dynasty Vanguard, forcing them to retreat and recuperate. With the PDV seemingly out of the way, the TSFMC is now focusing on bringing the Colossus sector under Solarian law by force and neutralising anything that stands between them and their conquest. Meanwhile, the PDV has begun a theocratic insurgency to repel the Solarian heathens in the glorious name of the Sultan, no matter the cost.
[bold][color=red]Total war[/color][/bold] is declared between the TSFMC and PDV only if both the [color=blue]TSFMC Colonel[/color] and [color=tan]PDV Grand Vizier[/color] activate their war declarators.
Insurgency is always available to vote, and is the only gamemode with no voting weight.
## Biothreat (TSF OR PDV, 3hr)
TSF: [italic][color=yellow]After successfully laying claim to the Colossus sector, the Federation struggles to keep it stable while a devasting bio-weapon wreaks havoc within it.[/color][/italic]
PDV: [italic][color=yellow]After successfully driving off the Federation, the Dynasty now must survive the aftermath as a devastating bio-weapon wreaks havoc in the Colossus Sector.[/color][/italic]
[bold]Biothreat[/bold] is an alternative gamemode featuring only one of the two major military powers.
As opposed to the war during Insurgency, the main threat during Biothreat is the overwhelming presence of chimera fleshbeasts flying into the sector with infected vessels missing their transponders. During Biothreat, the shield on [color=blue]TSFMC Flagship Halcyon[/color] or [color=tan]PDV Helios Fortress[/color] has been replaced with an experimental version of the [color=green]Biodome[/color]. The Biodome is a shield which kills any chimera that enter it. However, it has a glaring downside: it requires exponentially more power to operate, meaning the inhabitants of the station must eventually choose between producing exorbitant amounts of power or living without it.
[bold][color=red]Total war[/color][/bold] is never declared. Letoferol doesn't hold itself to any kind of agreement.
Biothreat requires at least 30 players. Biothreat has a [bold]50%[/bold] voting weight, meaning that it takes 2 players to vote it for 1 vote to be added to its total.
## Apocalypse (TSF|PDV, 3hr)
[italic][color=yellow]The TSFMC and PDV declare total war at the same time as a Letoferol outbreak. A battleground on all fronts.[/color][/italic]
[bold]Apocalypse[/bold] is hell on all fronts, offering a much faster-paced and bloody version of Insurgency.
Tensions rise rapidly as both the Trans-Solarian Federation and Phaeton Dynasty accuse each other of starting a Letoferol outbreak. As negotiations fall apart, total war is declared, leaving civilians to fend for themselves with death at every corner.
[bold][color=red]Total war[/color][/bold] is declared between the TSFMC and PDV at 01:00:00 on the dot.
Apocalypse requires at least 30 players. Apocalypse has a [bold]25%[/bold] voting weight, meaning that it takes 4 players to vote it for 1 vote to be added to its total.
## Hyperwar (TSF|PDV ONLY, 3hr)
[italic][color=yellow]The TSFMC and PDV declare total war while all civilians wisely retreat far away from the warzone.[/color][/italic]
[bold]Hyperwar[/bold] is a full on brawl with no bystanders.
During Hyperwar, both the TSFMC and PDV are provided with a [bold]nuclear fission explosive[/bold] and all points of interest, with the sole exceptions of [color=blue]TSFMC Flagship Halcyon[/color] and [color=tan]PDV Helios Fortress[/color], are removed. Both Halcyon and Helios are significantly upgunned, their passive research gain is increased from 35/s to 200/s, and they automatically produce plastitanium, cloth, durathread and (for PDV) data chits over time. Instead of INSO-357k or LINEAR-21, there is a singular asteroid ring 12 kilometres away from the center of the sector to gain materials from. The round's victor is determined by whichever side manages to set off the nuke on their enemy's base first.
[bold][color=red]Total war[/color][/bold] is declared between the TSFMC and PDV at 02:00:00 on the dot.
Hyperwar requires at least 30 players. Hyperwar has a [bold]15%[/bold] voting weight, meaning that it takes around 7 players to vote it for 1 vote to be added to its total.
## Crocus (TSF|PDV, 1hr)
[italic][color=yellow]A TSF garrison must defend against an invading PDV force for 1 hour. One planet map only, no ships.[/color][/italic]
[bold]Crocus[/bold] is a short scenario featuring on-planet warfare.
The Trans-Solarian Federation receives an anonymous tip about an impending Phaethon attack on the Jianghui Industrial Zone on the planet Crocus, and manages to deploy a garrison only ten minutes before the attack begins. The Federation must protect their beacons, their nanite canisters and their infantry's PDAs from the Dynasty. Additionally, they have been given an order to take the opportunity to seize as many Dynasty PDAs as they can for research purposes. This conflict leaves the Jianghui dockworkers on shift that day running, hiding or fighting for their lives in the crossfire. The round's victor is determined by whichever side gets the higher total progress on both of their objectives.
Crocus requires at least 30 players. Crocus has a [bold]25%[/bold] voting weight, meaning that it takes 4 players to vote it for 1 vote to be added to its total.
